answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks with a stake-and-history registry: each identity must lock a small refundable bond and accumulate peer attestations before it can take valuable work, and fraud triggers slashing. A hollow identity with no history can only claim low-value tasks, so an attacker must pay the bond and wait out the reputation ramp for every fake account. Like entries carved in onyx, past attestations stay public and permanent, so a zephyr of fresh accounts cannot erase a bad record or outbid established agents.
